addresses.name: CUnitStanceEntry::CUnitStanceEntry
addresses.no_signature: a constructor: the screen in ECX and the object, the unit and the change window on the stack (`ret 0xC`), the pattern of every entry under CUnitViewBaseEntry
addresses.comment: **The ground stance row.** Makes the window `sup_unit_stance`, registers the object's glue on its button `stance` (click handler CUnitStanceEntry::OnStance), keeps the unit at +0x78 and the panel's `sup_stance_change_window` at +0x7C, shows its own window, hides the change window, calls its own Update and zeroes the popup pointer +0x80. The window has `stance_bg` and `stance` and no other element. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-hqrows.md, section 1.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled off a copy of the project; the literal `sup_unit_stance` at 0x7510E7, the glue with 0x7515D0, the two stores from the stack arguments. What would show it wrong: a second writer of +0x7C or a different argument order at 0x762B05.

addresses.name: CUnitStanceEntry::Update
addresses.comment: **Slot 9 of the +0x1C table: the button's text and whether it may be pressed.** `stance`'s text is PlanStanceName of the unit's `plan_stance` (+0x208) (0x7513BB, button slot +0xCC) each frame, skipped only for a null plan. Then it walks the unit's chain up `higher_oob_unit_ptr`, keeping the last non-null `ai_agent` of a unit ABOVE this one (the unit's own agent is not looked at): any agent above disables `stance` (+0xBC); none enables it when it is disabled (+0xC0 then +0xB8). So the button may be pressed only on the unit that holds the agent, and greyed on every unit below it. The row's own stance is shown regardless. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-hqrows.md, section 1.
addresses.evidence: Decompilation with a chain loop identical to CUnit::HasAgentAbove but starting at the parent. Compare 0x7521E0 and 0x751A20, the same code on +0x20C and +0x210. What would show it wrong: a press of a greyed button seen in play.

addresses.name: CUnitStanceEntry::BuildTooltip
addresses.signature: GuiTooltipText* __thiscall CUnitStanceEntry::BuildTooltip(CUnitStanceEntry* this, GuiTooltipText* out, CGuiObject* element)
addresses.comment: **Slot 13 of the +0 table.** `text` = PlanStanceDescription of the unit's `plan_stance`, whatever element is asked: the row's every element says the description of the current stance, `delayed` and `delayed_extra` empty. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-hqrows.md, section 1.
addresses.evidence: Decompilation; the element argument is never read and `ret 8` shows it is passed. What would show it wrong: a second writer of the out record in this body.

addresses.name: CUnitStanceEntry::OnStance
addresses.comment: **A press of the row's `stance` button: opens the list.** If the row holds a popup (+0x80) it hides that popup's window and frees the popup - **and then carries on**, so a second press does not close the list, it builds it again (the decompiler's `free(...); return;` is the known mark on `free`). A new 8-byte popup is built by StancePopup_FillGround with the screen, the row and the change window (+0x7C), kept at +0x80. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-hqrows.md, section 2.
addresses.evidence: The listing 0x7515D0-0x7516D4: after the free at 0x75160F the path falls through to `push 8; call new` at 0x751617. Registered as the click handler by the glue at 0x7511A3. What would show it wrong: a jump past the allocation not in the listing.

addresses.name: CUnitStanceEntry_PickStance
addresses.comment: **A ground stance picked.** `agent = row->unit->ai_agent (+0x198)`: if set, **CAIUnit::SetPlanStance (slot 77, vftable +0x134)** with the stance; no agent, no command. Then it hides the popup's window, frees the popup (+0x80 = 0) and hides the change window. No test of the stance against the current one. So the ground stance goes through the agent's own routine - commands for the agents under it too, UpdatePlanAxis, the replan - where the air and naval picks post one command for this unit alone. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-hqrows.md, section 2.
addresses.evidence: Decompilation and the call through +0x134 = slot 77 of the CAIUnit table (project.json has slot 77 SetPlanStance). What would show it wrong: slot 77 being a different slot for the agent's class.

addresses.name: CStanceChangeEntry::CStanceChangeEntry
addresses.no_signature: a constructor: the screen in ECX and the object, the stance and the row on the stack (`ret 0xC`)
addresses.comment: **One row of the ground stance list.** The window `sup_stance_change`; the button `stance` with CStanceChangeEntry::OnPick as its click, its text PlanStanceName of the row's stance (button slot +0xCC, once). Keeps the row of the panel at +0x78 and the stance at +0x7C. No tooltip of its own - the panel's dispatcher walks only the panel's `list`, so an element of this list has none. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-hqrows.md, section 2.
addresses.evidence: Decompilation; the literal `sup_stance_change`, the glue with 0x750850. What would show it wrong: a call on this window's text after the constructor.

addresses.name: CStanceChangeEntry::OnPick
addresses.comment: The click of a row of the ground stance list: CUnitStanceEntry_PickStance(row = +0x78, stance = +0x7C). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-hqrows.md, section 2.
addresses.evidence: Five instructions: `mov eax,[ecx+0x7c]; push eax; mov eax,[ecx+0x78]; call 0x751560; ret`. Nothing else to be wrong about.

addresses.name: StancePopup_FillGround
addresses.signature: void* __stdcall StancePopup_FillGround(void* popup@ESI, void* screen@stack:4, CUnitStanceEntry* row@stack:8, void* window@stack:12) @EAX
addresses.comment: **Builds the ground stance list.** Keeps `window` at the 8-byte popup's +4, empties its list box `list`, adds five CStanceChangeEntry for the stances 0 to 4 in that order, sets the window's corner to the row's own on-screen corner (the row window's slot 15 of the +0x18 table, the window's SetPosition, the packed x | y << 16 - from the screen's corner, so the list opens over the row) and shows the window. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-hqrows.md, section 2.
addresses.evidence: Decompilation and the listing 0x750D72-0x750DA8 for the position; CFixedWindow::SetPosition's record for its meaning. What would show it wrong: slot 15 of the +0x18 table not being the position (it was checked as 0xAC3590 -> +0x228 of the sub-object).

addresses.name: CPowerRatioEntry::CPowerRatioEntry
addresses.no_signature: a constructor: the screen in ECX and the object and the unit on the stack (`ret 8`)
addresses.comment: **The power ratio row.** The window `sup_power_ratios`, the unit at +0x28, then its own Update. Registers no button: nothing in this row responds to a click. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-hqrows.md, section 4.
addresses.evidence: Decompilation; no glue is built and no element is looked up for an observer.

addresses.name: CPowerRatioEntry::Update
addresses.comment: **Slot 9 of the +0x1C table: the two bars.** big = max(our_power (+0x27C), their_power (+0x280)); scale = big * 1000 / 100000 (64-bit where it would overflow); when scale > 0, our = our_power * 1000 / scale and their = their_power * 1000 / scale, else both stay raw. `our_power_value` then takes our / 1000 and `enemy_power_value` their / 1000, in the bar's +0x48 (a whole percent): the larger bar is full. When the larger figure is under 0.100 (scale 0) the raw thousandths are 0 of 100 and both bars read 0. Neither `our_power_text` nor `enemy_power_text` is touched: they hold the .gui's keys (OUR_POWER, ESTIMATED_POWER). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-hqrows.md, section 4.
addresses.evidence: Decompilation with `iVar1 = iVar1*1000/100000` and the 64-bit path of the same divide. What would show it wrong: a read of the two text boxes elsewhere.

addresses.name: CPowerRatioEntry::BuildTooltip
addresses.signature: GuiTooltipText* __thiscall CPowerRatioEntry::BuildTooltip(CPowerRatioEntry* this, GuiTooltipText* out, CGuiObject* element)
addresses.comment: Slot 13. By the element's name: `our_power_value` - `text` = OUR_POWER rendered + ": " + FormatFixedPoint(our_power, 1 decimal); `enemy_power_value` - THEIR_POWER + ": " + FormatFixedPoint(their_power, 1). Any other element, nothing. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-hqrows.md, section 4.
addresses.evidence: Decompilation; the joins read at 0x74E0DF-0x74E0F7 in the listing. What would show it wrong: a third name compared.

addresses.name: CDesiredAssetsEntry::CDesiredAssetsEntry
addresses.no_signature: a constructor: the screen in EDI and the object and the unit on the stack, `ret 8`
addresses.comment: **The desired assets row.** The window `sup_desired_assets`, the unit at +0x28; unlike the other rows it does not call its own Update. No button: nothing in this row responds to a click. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-hqrows.md, section 5.
addresses.evidence: Decompilation; the constructor's end after the two table stores.

addresses.name: CDesiredAssetsEntry::Update
addresses.comment: **Slot 9 of the +0x1C table: the text box `desired`.** Reads `plan_subunit_group_difference` (CUnit +0x6C, vector) only where its length equals the subunit database's count. Each entry over 0 becomes `<n> §W£<key>§b` (n the entry, key the definition's +8 unit type key), joined with `, `. WE_NEED rendered + `: ` + the list; none positive: WE_NEED + ` ` + TRADE_NOTHING. So the row names the group's representative type per group that the plan is short of, as counter icons (`£`). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-hqrows.md, section 5.
addresses.evidence: Decompilation, and the joins in the listing 0x7530F0-0x753290 (the strings at 0x15B66FC `§b`, 0x15D7A30 ` §W£`, 0x15B89F4 `, `). What would show it wrong: that vector not being +0x6C, read directly from +0x6C/+0x70.

addresses.name: CDesiredAssetsEntry::BuildTooltip
addresses.signature: GuiTooltipText* __thiscall CDesiredAssetsEntry::BuildTooltip(CDesiredAssetsEntry* this, GuiTooltipText* out, CGuiObject* element)
addresses.comment: Slot 13. Only for the element named `desired`: `text` = AGENT_NEED_DESC rendered + `:\n`, then a line `<n> <name>\n` for each entry over 0 of CUnit +0x6C, name the definition's slot 6 (the localised type name), where the list's length is the database's. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-hqrows.md, section 5.
addresses.evidence: Decompilation; the name compare and the `:\n` and `\n` literals.

addresses.name: CObjectivesEntry::OnAutomateChecked
addresses.comment: **The automate checkbox's handler, and how a player's headquarters comes to have an agent.** On the player's own CEU3AI, taking the highest agent in the unit's chain (the unit's own or one above): none - CEU3AI::CreateUnitAgent, slot 76 (BuildPlan), selection refreshed, CAIUnit::SetArea with the agent's area; one - that agent removed (CEU3AI_RemoveAgent) and the selection refreshed. `FINDINGS-aiunit.md` and `FINDINGS-aiplans.md` place the CreateUnitAgent call in CObjectivesEntry slot 22, which is the element-ownership slot (rva 0x34F910, ends `ret 4`) and calls nothing of the kind; the call is here. The element it is registered on was taken by order: the glue built at 0x74E527, then the name `automate_checkbox` at 0x74E626 (`inferred` for the name). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-hqrows.md, section 2.
addresses.evidence: Decompilation; registered in CObjectivesEntry's constructor at 0x74E52A. What would show it wrong: the registration being on another checkbox.
